Package hadur2.core.move

Class OurBullet

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.move.OurBullet
public final class OurBullet extends Object
One of our bullets in flight, as the core fired it: it leaves from where we stood on the tick we fired, along the gun's heading that tick, and after turn k it is speed * (k - fireTime) from there (the engine's order, checked in S2's bench).

MOVE-1 needs our bullets' paths to work out where they shadow the enemy's waves (BulletShadows). A bullet flies in a straight line at a constant speed, so its fire time, source, heading and power pin down its whole path and nothing needs updating while it flies. HadurCore creates one when the gun fires and hands it to MoveController.ourBulletFired(hadur2.core.move.OurBullet); the engine's bullet events later remove it through MoveController.ourBulletGone(double, double).

Coordinates are Robocode's: x to the right, y up, in px; headings are in radians with 0 pointing north (+y) and angles growing clockwise, so a step of length d along heading h moves (d sin h, d cos h). Instances are immutable.

  • Method Details

    • at

      public Point2D.Double at(long time)
      Where the bullet is after turn time: speed * (time - fireTime) px from source along heading. Times before fireTime give points behind the source; callers only ask for times from fireTime on.
      Parameters:
      time - the turn, in ticks
      Returns:
      a new point, in px

    • is

      public boolean is(double heading, double power)
      Whether this is the bullet an engine event names by its heading and power. Both are compared to within 1e-6, a tolerance for rounding on the way through the adapter. Two bullets in flight that match the same event are not told apart: MoveController.ourBulletGone(double, double) drops the oldest.
      Parameters:
      heading - the event bullet's heading, in radians
      power - the event bullet's power
      Returns:
      true when both match this bullet's
